          brisk_walk 2m
        main:

            push_up 30s
            rest 15s

            high_knees 30s
            rest 15s

            rest 15s

            rest 15s
            lateral_bound_left 15s
            rest 15s
        cooldown:
          quad_stretch 60 seconds

      DAY Monday training 45m "Lower/upper - Week 3":
        warmup:
          cycling 5m
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          barbell_row 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          hip_bridge 3x12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cardio:
          cycling 12m
        cooldown:
          glute_stretch 60 seconds
          thoracic_extension 60 seconds

NUTRITION
  PLAN "Anti-Inflammatory Eating for Endometriosis Support"
  TYPE nutrition
  VISIBILITY public

  GUIDELINES
    - Emphasize whole foods with emphasis on plants, lean proteins, and healthy fats.
    - Prioritize foods high in omega-3s and polyphenols; limit omega-6 rich processed fats.
    - Favor unprocessed carbohydrates with fiber; moderate overall carbohydrate intake around training.
    - Hydration: 2.0–2.5 liters/day baseline; add water with meals and around training.
    - Gluten-containing foods only as tolerated; consider a gluten-free phase if sensitivity observed.
    - Limit added sugars and ultra-processed foods; minimize alcohol consumption.

  DAILY_MACROS
    - Protein: 1.6–2.0 g per kg body weight
    - Fat: 25–35% of total daily calories, with emphasis on monounsaturated and omega-3 fats
    - Carbohydrates: remainder of calories from complex, low-glycemic sources

  FOOD_SOURCES
    - Anti-inflammatory staples:
      - fatty fish (salmon, sardines) 2–3 servings/week
      - extra virgin olive oil; nuts and seeds (almonds, walnuts, flaxseed)
      - leafy greens (spinach, kale), cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cauliflower)
      - berries (blueberries, strawberries), cherries
      - turmeric (+ black pepper), ginger
      - colorful vegetables (bell peppers, carrots)
      - whole grains (quinoa, oats, brown rice) as tolerated
    - Protein options:
      - chicken, turkey, lean beef, eggs, legumes (as tolerated)
      - dairy or fortified alternatives if tolerated
    - Hydration boosters:
      - herbal teas; water with lemon; unsweetened beverages

  MEAL_STRUCTURE
    - Pre-workout (60–90 minutes before): balanced meal with protein and complex carbs (e.g., Greek yogurt with berries and oats)
    - Post-workout: protein-rich snack within 1–2 hours (e.g., protein shake with a piece of fruit or tuna on whole-grain toast)
    - Breakfast: focus on protein, fiber, and healthy fats
    - Lunch/Dinner: vegetables + lean protein + whole grains + healthy fats
    - Snack options: fruit, nuts, yogurt, hummus with veggies

  INFLAMMATION_MODIFIERS
    - Foods to emphasize: salmon, salmon oil or algae oil, sardines; berries; leafy greens; turmeric; ginger; green tea
    - Foods to limit or avoid during flare windows:
      - highly processed foods, added sugars, excessive saturated fats
      - excessive alcohol
      - processed meats
    - Phased timing around flare windows:
      - during flare days: prioritize anti-inflammatory meals, keep portions moderate, ensure adequate protein and fiber
      - during non-flare days: maintain consistent protein intake and fiber to support recovery

  SUPPLEMENTATION (optional; consult clinician)
    - Omega-3 supplement if dietary intake is insufficient
    - Vitamin D3 1000–4000 IU/day depending on serum levels
    - Magnesium 200–400 mg in the evening if cramping or sleep lines up
    - Probiotic with multiple strains if digestive symptoms are present

  END_TEST_PLAN
  1RM_TEST
    - CONDITION: Phase 3 end of program
    - PLAN: If medically cleared, perform a 1RM test for select priority lifts (squat, bench_press, deadlift if included, or row variations) in a controlled, non-exhaustive session
    - SAFETY: ensure proper warmup, technique work, spotters as needed, and RPE guidance; avoid using Valsalva with endometriosis considerations
    - SETUP: test only after full Phase 2 completion and before any Phase 3 deload ( Phase 3 is 0 weeks, but 1RM can be appended as a final assessment)
    - NOTES: use progression approach (e.g., estimated 1RM or multiple attempts to find 1RM within a single session) and record 1RM for future planning

END PLAN
